# `pilecap.files`

<!-- generated by `python -m quality.sdk --reference`; edit the source, never this -->

17 exports. Import them as `from pilecap.files import <name>`.

### `pilecap.files.FILE_ARCHIVED`

A document has been taken out of the working set. Payload: `schemas.StoredFileOut` — the document as every read door reports it, with `archived_at` now set, so a subscriber can see WHEN as well as THAT. Emitted inside `archive_file`'s transaction, so an archive that rolled back said nothing.

- value · source `apps/files/events.py:57`

### `pilecap.files.FILE_MOVED`

The event name `files.file.moved`.

- value · source `apps/files/events.py:67`

### `pilecap.files.FILE_RESTORED`

An archived document is back in the working set. Payload: `schemas.StoredFileOut` with `archived_at` and `archived_by` null again. Emitted inside `restore_file`'s transaction, and only when the call changed the row — restoring a live document says nothing. A subscriber may conclude the document is listed again; nothing about its versions or its bytes moved in either direction, because archive never touched them.

- value · source `apps/files/events.py:65`

### `pilecap.files.FILE_STORED`

One version's bytes are in the store, measured and recorded. Payload: `schemas.FileStoredOut` — the document as every read door reports it, plus the version that just landed with its digest and its size. Emitted inside `record_stored`'s transaction, so a finalize that rolled back said nothing.

- value · source `apps/files/events.py:50`
